randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] Constants\nconstexpr double MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR = 0.02;\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: fill\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Initialize array ****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: verifyResults\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Verifies correctness of results by comparing to reference solution\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   reference: array holding the reference result vector\n//   result: array holding the result vector to verify\n//   size: number of elements per vector\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nbool verifyResults(const double* reference, const double* result, const index_t size) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) {\n        const double ref = reference[i];\n        const double res = result[i];\n        if (std::abs(ref) < 1e-10) {\n            // For very small values, check absolute error\n            if (std::abs(res) > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e\\n\", i, ref, res);\n                return false;\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Check relative error\n            const double relError = std::abs((res - ref) / ref);\n            if (relError > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e (rel error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, ref, res, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -m <val>     Maximum value for matrix and vector elements (default: 1.0)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    index_t numRows = 1024;\n    index_t sparsity = 10;\n    index_t iterations = 10;\n    double maxVal = 1.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numRows = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            sparsity = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-m\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            maxVal = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Calculate number of non-zero elements\n    const index_t nItems = (numRows * numRows) / sparsity;\n\n    printf(\"Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %u x %u\\n\", numRows, numRows);\n    printf(\"Sparsity: 1 out of %u entries is non-zero\\n\", sparsity);\n    printf(\"Non-zero elements: %u (%.2f%% sparse)\\n\", \n           nItems, 100.0 * (1.0 - static_cast<double>(nItems) / (numRows * numRows)));\n    printf(\"Iterations: %u\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Max value: %.2f\\n\", maxVal);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Allocate and initialize data structures\n    std::vector<double> h_val(nItems);                  // Non-zero values\n    std::vector<index_t> h_cols(nItems);                // Column indices\n    std::vector<index_t> h_rowDelimiters(numRows + 1);  // Row delimiters\n    std::vector<double> h_vec(numRows); iter < iterations; ++iter) {\n        spmvCpu(h_val.data(), h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(),\n                h_vec.data(), numRows, h_out.data());\n    }\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate performance metrics\n    const double gflops = (2.0 * nItems * iterations) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    const double avgTime = duration.count() / static_cast<double>(iterations);\n    \n    printf(\"Average time per iteration: %.3f ms\\n\", avgTime);\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(h_out, \"OutputVector\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        const bool valid = verifyResults(h_reference.data(), h_out.data(), numRows);\n\n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return 0;\n}\nhash.hpp\nresults_output.hpp\n#pragma once\n\n#include <cstdint>\n\n// FNV-1a hash, 64 bit length\nclass hash {\n  public:\n\tusing digest = uint64_t;\n\n\ttemplate <typename T>\n\tvoid add(const T& value) {\n\t\tconst unsigned char* bytes = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(&value);\n\t\tfor(size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(T); ++i) {\n\t\t\td = (d ^ bytes[i]) * 0x100000001b3ull;\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tdigest get() const { return d; }\n\n  private:\n\tdigest d = 0xcbf29ce484222325ull;\n};\n#pragma once\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <cinttypes>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"hash.hpp\"\n\n// Kahan summation for numerically stable sum\ntemplate <typename T>\nT kahan_sum(const std::vector<T>& data) {\n    T sum = 0.0;\n    T c = 0.0;\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        T y = val - c;\n        T t = sum + y;\n        c = (t - sum) - y;\n        sum = t;\n    }\n    return sum;\n}\n\n// Print results for floating-point arrays\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid print_results(const std::vector<T>& data, const char* name = \"Result\") {\n    if (data.empty()) {\n        printf(\"=== RESULTS ===\\n\");\n        printf(\"Name: %s\\n\", name);\n        printf(\"Elements: 0\\n\");\n        printf(\"=== END RESULTS ===\\n\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const size_t N = data.size();\n    \n    // Compute statistics\n    T sum = kahan_sum(data);\n    T min_val = data[0];\n    T max_val = data[0];\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        min_val = std::min(min_val, val);\n        max_val = std::max(max_val, val);\n    }\n    \n    // Compute hash\n    hash h;\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        h.add(val);\n    }\n    \n    // Sample indices: 0, N/4, N/2, 3N/4, N-1\n    size_t indices[5] = {0, N/4, N/2, 3*N/4, N-1};\n    \n    printf(\"=== RESULTS ===\\n\");\n    printf(\"Name: %s\\n\", name);\n    printf(\"Elements: %zu\\n\", N);\n    printf(\"Sum: %.17e\\n\", static_cast<double>(sum));\n    printf(\"Min: %.17e\\n\", static_cast<double>(min_val));\n    printf(\"Max: %.17e\\n\", static_cast<double>(max_val));\n    for (int i = 0; i < 5; ++i) {\n        printf(\"Sample[%zu]: %.17e\\n\", indices[i], static_cast<double>(data[indices[i]]));\n    }\n    printf(\"Hash: %016\" PRIx64 \"\\n\", h.get());\n    printf(\"=== END RESULTS ===\\n\");\n}\n\n// Print results for integer arrays (uses exact hash comparison)\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid print_results_int(const std::vector<T>& data, const char* name = \"Result\") {\n    if (data.empty()) {\n        printf(\"=== RESULTS ===\\n\");\n        printf(\"Name: %s\\n\", name);\n        printf(\"Elements: 0\\n\");\n        printf(\"=== END RESULTS ===\\n\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const size_t N = data.size();\n    \n    // Compute hash\n    hash h;\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        h.add(val);\n    }\n    \n    // Compute min/max\n    T min_val = data[0];\n    T max_val = data[0];\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        min_val = std::min(min_val, val);\n        max_val = std::max(max_val, val);\n    }\n    \n    // Sample indices: 0, N/4, N/2, 3N/4, N-1\n    size_t indices[5] = {0, N/4, N/2, 3*N/4, N-1};\n    \n    printf(\"=== RESULTS ===\\n\");\n    printf(\"Name: %s\\n\", name);\n    printf(\"Elements: %zu\\n\", N);\n    printf(\"Min: %lld\\n\", static_cast<long long>(min_val));\n    printf(\"Max: %lld\\n\", static_cast<long long>(max_val));\n    for (int i = 0; around.\n\nFor the CPU SpMV baseline, I'm parallelizing the row loop with OpenMP static scheduling, accumulating each row's dot product sequentially within the thread.\n\nNow I'm writing the scalar CUDA kernel that assigns rows to threads in a grid-stride loop, each thread summing products of matrix values and vector entries across its row's column range.\n\nFor the vector kernel, I'm assigning a full warp per row, having each lane stride through the row's nonzeros, then performing a warp shuffle reduction so lane 0 writes the final dot product.\n\nNow I'm sizing the launch configuration, picking 256 threads per block and capping the grid size based on the row count to balance occupancy against overhead.\n\nChecking that rd uses uint32_t consistent with index_t, then matching the host's fill order for the root vector and setting up the non-root receive buffer sized to rows+1.\n\nRoot then sends each rank its row delimiters, values, and columns using the chunked send helper, and I need to make sure zero-nnz ranks still work correctly when the chunk count is zero.\n\nI'm setting up root's non-blocking sends to each rank followed by Waitall before data is used, then handling device uploads with cudaMemcpy for the local values, columns, row pointers, and vector, broadcasting the vector to all ranks with proper allocation on non-root processes.\n\nSince command-line arguments are parsed identically on every rank, I realize nItems and numRows can be computed locally everywhere without needing to broadcast them separately — only the actual matrix data (val/cols/rowDelimiters) is root-exclusive and needs distribution.\n\nI'm now outlining the full program structure: MPI_Init before argument parsing, root-only usage/error printing with all ranks returning cleanly, and the necessary includes for MPI, OpenMP, CUDA runtime, and standard headers.\n\nWriting the hybrid implementation...\n\nAdding chunked receive and broadcast helpers for the two data types, then starting the partition computation function...\n\nI confirm the partition logic works correctly since each row range maps to roughly equal nnz counts, with the last boundary guaranteed valid. Now I'm sketching out main: initializing MPI, parsing arguments with error handling that prints and finalizes cleanly on root, computing item counts, and printing the startup banner.\n\nI'm setting up GPU binding, then building the data structures: on root only, allocating value/column/row-descriptor arrays and filling them via random matrix initialization, then computing the row partition boundaries. These bounds get broadcast to all ranks along with a chunked vector broadcast, after which each rank determines its local row range and sets up non-blocking requests to scatter rows from root to each worker.\n\nStill writing data distribution logic...\n\nStill computing local row ranges...\n\nNow I'm setting up GPU assignment by splitting the MPI communicator into shared-memory groups to determine each rank's local GPU index.\n\nDevice allocation...\n\nI'm also preparing a CPU reference implementation to validate the GPU SpMV results against, using the local row data before timing begins.\n\nI'm weighing whether a hybrid CPU+GPU split makes sense given the 256-thread host versus the RTX 3090's bandwidth advantage — it could add meaningful throughput but introduces real complexity, and the prompt's guidance to combine MPI, OpenMP, and CUDA \"as appropriate\" suggests it's worth considering rather than mandatory.\n\nI'm leaning toward keeping compute strictly GPU-side and documenting that choice clearly, since finding an optimal fixed split ratio between host and device is hard to justify without deeper benchmarking, and other OpenMP use cases like root-side data generation don't parallelize cleanly without altering the RNG.\n\nNow I'm structuring the timing logic: doing an untimed warm-up kernel launch, syncing, barrier, then timing the actual iteration loop, synchronizing again, and reducing each rank's local elapsed time with an MPI max reduction so I capture the slowest process. I'm also handling the gather step, copying device output back to host only when there are rows to process, skipping it otherwise.\n\nI'm working out the MPI_Gatherv setup with per-rank counts and displacements as ints, confirming the sizes stay within int range, then deciding how the root prints results, matches the original's millisecond formatting, and computes Gflops from the timing data while being careful about the division-by-zero edge case when elapsed time rounds to zero. {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793018296500,"sessionID":"ses_e87ca63e6ffe4sSp3dJLurE0Ex","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01QKeSH9DvZAGLkwXTvHX4n9","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/spmv_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r2/spmv/spmv.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA sparse matrix-vector multiplication benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   MPI:    rows are split into contiguous blocks, one per rank, with block\n//           boundaries chosen so every rank owns a similar number of nonzeros.\n//           Rank 0 generates the matrix and vector exactly as the sequential\n//           original did (the rand() sequence defines the data), then\n//           distributes the blocks. The vector is replicated on all ranks and\n//           the output blocks are gathered back to rank 0.\n//   CUDA:   each rank binds to one GPU (node-local rank modulo device count)\n//           and computes its row block with a CSR kernel. The local matrix\n//           block is uploaded once, before timing.\n//   OpenMP: the host-side reference computation used for validation is\n//           parallelized over the rows of each rank's block.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdint>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nusing index_t = uint32_t;\n\n// Constants\nconstexpr double MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR = 0.02;\nconstexpr int TAG_ROWDELIM = 1;\nconstexpr int TAG_VAL = 2;\nconstexpr int TAG_COLS = 3;\nconstexpr size_t MPI_CHUNK = size_t(1) << 30;  // max elements per MPI message\nconstexpr int CUDA_BLOCK = 256;\nconstexpr index_t VECTOR_KERNEL_MIN_AVG_NNZ = 8;\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                               \\\n    do {                                                                               \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                     \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                     \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,           \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                         \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                              \\\n        }                                                                              \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: fill\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Initialize array with random values\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   A: pointer to the array to initialize\n//   n: number of elements in the array\n//   maxVal: specifies range of random values [0, maxVal]\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format.\n//   Rows are independent, so they are distributed across OpenMP threads.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Kernel: spmvScalarKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   CSR SpMV with one thread per row. Used when rows are very short, since a\n//   warp per row would leave most lanes idle.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvScalarKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                                 const index_t* __restrict__ rowDelimiters,\n                                 const double* __restrict__ vec, const index_t rows,\n                                 double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const size_t stride = static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.x) * blockDim.x;\n    for (size_t row = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; row < rows;\n         row += stride) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        const index_t end = rowDelimiters[row + 1];\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[row]; j < end; ++j) {\n            t += val[j] * vec[cols[j]];\n        }\n        out[row] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Kernel: spmvVectorKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   CSR SpMV with one warp per row. Lanes stride over the row's nonzeros so\n//   that accesses to val/cols are coalesced, followed by a warp shuffle\n//   reduction.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvVectorKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                                 const index_t* __restrict__ rowDelimiters,\n                                 const double* __restrict__ vec, const index_t rows,\n                                 double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const index_t lane = threadIdx.x & 31;\n    const size_t warpsInGrid = (static_cast<size_t>(gridDim.x) * blockDim.x) >> 5;\n    for (size_t row = (static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) >> 5;\n         row < rows; row += warpsInGrid) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        const index_t end = rowDelimiters[row + 1];\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[row] + lane; j < end; j += 32) {\n            t += val[j] * vec[cols[j]];\n        }\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int offset = 16; offset > 0; offset >>= 1) {\n            t += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, t, offset);\n        }\n        if (lane == 0) {\n            out[row] = t;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: verifyResults\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Verifies correctness of results by comparing to reference solution\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   reference: array holding the reference result vector\n//   result: array holding the result vector to verify\n//   size: number of elements per vector\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nbool verifyResults(const double* reference, const double* result, const index_t size) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < size; ++i) {\n        const double ref = reference[i];\n        const double res = result[i];\n        if (std::abs(ref) < 1e-10) {\n            // For very small values, check absolute error\n            if (std::abs(res) > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e\\n\", i, ref, res);\n                return false;\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Check relative error\n            const double relError = std::abs((res - ref) / ref);\n            if (relError > MAX_RELATIVE_ERROR) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e (rel error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, ref, res, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: computeRowPartition\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Splits rows into `parts` contiguous blocks with roughly equal nonzero\n//   counts. Block p owns rows [bounds[p], bounds[p+1]).\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nstd::vector<index_t> computeRowPartition(const index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t dim,\n                                         const index_t nnz, const int parts) {\n    std::vector<index_t> bounds(parts + 1);\n    bounds[0] = 0;\n    bounds[parts] = dim;\n    for (int p = 1; p < parts; ++p) {\n        const index_t target = static_cast<index_t>(static_cast<uint64_t>(nnz) * p / parts);\n        const index_t* it = std::lower_bound(rowDelimiters, rowDelimiters + dim + 1, target);\n        index_t bound = static_cast<index_t>(it - rowDelimiters);\n        bounds[p] = std::max(bound, bounds[p - 1]);\n    }\n    return bounds;\n}\n\n// Sends `count` elements in MPI-sized chunks. Requests are completed by the caller.\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid sendChunked(const T* buf, size_t count, MPI_Datatype type, int dst, int tag,\n                 std::vector<MPI_Request>& reqs) {\n    for (size_t off = 0; off < count; off += MPI_CHUNK) {\n        const size_t n = std::min(MPI_CHUNK, count - off);\n        MPI_Request req;\n        MPI_Isend(buf + off, static_cast<int>(n), type, dst, tag, MPI_COMM_WORLD, &req);\n        reqs.push_back(req);\n    }\n}\n\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid recvChunked(T* buf, size_t count, MPI_Datatype type, int src, int tag) {\n    for (size_t off = 0; off < count; off += MPI_CHUNK) {\n        const size_t n = std::min(MPI_CHUNK, count - off);\n        MPI_Recv(buf + off, static_cast<int>(n), type, src, tag, MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_STATUS_IGNORE);\n    }\n}\n\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid bcastChunked(T* buf, size_t count, MPI_Datatype type) {\n    for (size_t off = 0; off < count; off += MPI_CHUNK) {\n        const size_t n = std::min(MPI_CHUNK, count - off);\n        MPI_Bcast(buf + off, static_cast<int>(n), type, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    }\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -m <val>     Maximum value for matrix and vector elements (default: 1.0)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0;\n    int numRanks = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &numRanks);\n    const bool root = (rank == 0);\n\n    index_t numRows = 1024;\n    index_t sparsity = 10;\n    index_t iterations = 10;\n    double maxVal = 1.0;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments (identical on every rank, so all ranks\n    // take the same exit path)\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numRows = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            sparsity = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-m\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            maxVal = atof(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (root) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (root) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            MPI_Finalize();\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Calculate number of non-zero elements\n    const index_t nItems = (numRows * numRows) / sparsity;\n\n    if (root) {\n        printf(\"Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %u x %u\\n\", numRows, numRows);\n        printf(\"Sparsity: 1 out of %u entries is non-zero\\n\", sparsity);\n        printf(\"Non-zero elements: %u (%.2f%% sparse)\\n\", \n               nItems, 100.0 * (1.0 - static_cast<double>(nItems) / (numRows * numRows)));\n        printf(\"Iterations: %u\\n\", iterations);\n        printf(\"Max value: %.2f\\n\", maxVal);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n        printf(\"MPI ranks: %d, OpenMP threads per rank: %d\\n\", numRanks, omp_get_max_threads());\n    }\n\n    // Generate the matrix and vector on rank 0 (sequential, same RNG order as the original)\n    std::vector<double> h_vec(numRows);                 // Dense vector (replicated on all ranks)\n    std::vector<double> h_val;                          // Non-zero values (root only)\n    std::vector<index_t> h_cols;                        // Column indices (root only)\n    std::vector<index_t> h_rowDelimiters;               // Row delimiters (root only)\n    std::vector<index_t> bounds(numRanks + 1);          // Row block boundaries\n\n    if (root) {\n        h_val.resize(nItems);\n        h_cols.resize(nItems);\n        h_rowDelimiters.resize(numRows + 1);\n\n        printf(\"Initializing data structures...\\n\");\n        fill(h_vec.data(), numRows, maxVal);\n        fill(h_val.data(), nItems, maxVal);\n        initRandomMatrix(h_cols.data(), h_rowDelimiters.data(), nItems, numRows);\n\n        bounds = computeRowPartition(h_rowDelimiters.data(), numRows, nItems, numRanks);\n    }\n    MPI_Bcast(bounds.data(), numRanks + 1, MPI_UINT32_T, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    bcastChunked(h_vec.data(), numRows, MPI_DOUBLE);\n\n    // Distribute row blocks from rank 0\n    const index_t rowBegin = bounds[rank];\n    const index_t rows = bounds[rank + 1] - rowBegin;\n    std::vector<index_t> localRowDelimiters(rows + 1);\n    std::vector<double> recvVal;\n    std::vector<index_t> recvCols;\n    const double* localVal = nullptr;\n    const index_t* localCols = nullptr;\n\n    if (root) {\n        std::vector<MPI_Request> reqs;\n        for (int p = 1; p < numRanks; ++p) {\n            const index_t r0 = bounds[p];\n            const index_t r1 = bounds[p + 1];\n            const index_t d0 = h_rowDelimiters[r0];\n            const index_t d1 = h_rowDelimiters[r1];\n            sendChunked(h_rowDelimiters.data() + r0, static_cast<size_t>(r1 - r0) + 1,\n                        MPI_UINT32_T, p, TAG_ROWDELIM, reqs);\n            sendChunked(h_val.data() + d0, d1 - d0, MPI_DOUBLE, p, TAG_VAL, reqs);\n            sendChunked(h_cols.data() + d0, d1 - d0, MPI_UINT32_T, p, TAG_COLS, reqs);\n        }\n\n        // Rank 0 uses its portion of the generated arrays directly\n        const index_t d0 = h_rowDelimiters[rowBegin];\n        for (index_t i = 0; i <= rows; ++i) {\n            localRowDelimiters[i] = h_rowDelimiters[rowBegin + i] - d0;\n        }\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793018357029,"sessionID":"ses_e87ca63e6ffe4sSp3dJLurE0Ex","part":{"id":"prt_17838cc6c0016Q6VUfa4ulA6Wc","messageID":"msg_17838c8ff0015CUYQHtbUc4n8Z","sessionID":"ses_e87ca63e6ffe4sSp3dJLurE0Ex","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing CMake is linking with the host g++ compiler from the CUDA toolkit rather than through nvcc, which seems to be because CMake defaults to the host compiler for linking CUDA device code.\n\nI think the fix is to drop the manual link option and rely on OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX, which should correctly supply the -fopenmp flag and gomp library at link time.\n\nSeparately, I'm puzzled why the architecture resolved to compute_52 instead of the native GPU architecture—possibly CMake 3.30 with nvcc 12.0 isn't properly detecting \"native\" and is falling back to a default value instead of reading the CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES variable as expected.\n\nSince the native detection seems unreliable, maybe I should fall back to an explicit architecture list covering common GPUs from Volta through Hopper, trading some extra compile time for broader compatibility.\n\n","time":{"start":1793018350700,"end":1793018357017},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793018357437,"sessionID":"ses_e87ca63e6ffe4sSp3dJLurE0Ex","part":{"id":"prt_17838e51d001dh5IVlNV2dseRY","messageID":"msg_17838c8ff0015CUYQHtbUc4n8Z","sessionID":"ses_e87ca63e6ffe4sSp3dJLurE0Ex","type":"text","text":"Two findings from the generated files: CMake links through the host `g++` (so the nvcc `-Xcompiler` link option is wrong), and `native` resolved to `compute_52`, which is a bad default for this GPU. I'm tracing through the allocAndCopy call for d_val, checking whether localVal and localNnz are computed correctly for the root case using the row delimiter offsets.\n\nWait, I think I found it: the generic lambda in allocAndCopy uses `remove_pointer_t` on a reference type (`double*&`), which doesn't strip the pointer as intended since references aren't pointers—so the element size calculation is subtly wrong. For doubles this coincidentally works since the sizes match, but for other types like uint32 it would overread host memory and cause exactly this kind of segfault on larger arrays. I'm rewriting allocAndCopy as a proper template function that takes a typed pointer and count directly, avoiding the decltype/remove_pointer trick entirely.\n\n","time":{"start":1793018527659,"end":1793018532756},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
